item.text: {"schema":"voice-draft-claim-audit/4","sentences":[{"id":"p1s1","status":"keep","reason":"This restates the request's imagined scenario: a system described by law as a narrow child-safety measure.","claims":[]},{"id":"p1s2","status":"disclose","reason":"The hypothetical legal description is consistent with the request, but the parenthetical asserts a usual statutory threshold not supplied there.","claims":[{"claim":"Online age-checking laws usually use eighteen or another legislatively specified age as the threshold.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Across the relevant online age-checking laws, what age thresholds are specified, and is eighteen usually the threshold?"}]},{"id":"p1s3","status":"keep","reason":"This states the essay's requested thesis as a possibility: machinery answering an age question can function more broadly as identity infrastructure.","claims":[]},{"id":"p1s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a concise conceptual distinction between a system's legal label and its functional design.","claims":[]},{"id":"p1s5","status":"disclose","reason":"The building metaphor restates possible expansion, but the final clause asserts a contingent pattern of institutional discovery and adoption.","claims":[{"claim":"Institutions are especially likely to expand an existing access-control mechanism once they discover that it exists.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence shows that institutional awareness of an existing access-control mechanism increases the likelihood that it will be adopted for additional uses?"}]},{"id":"p2s1","status":"keep","reason":"This characterizes the narrow age-checking concept through an illustrative transaction rather than reporting an actual implementation.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s2","status":"keep","reason":"Each listed decision is logically required to define an age-checking process: requester, acceptable evidence, verifier, and record handling.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s3","status":"keep","reason":"The conditional premise is explicit, and the conclusion follows conceptually because accounts, credentials, or recurring checks create functions beyond a one-time age determination.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s4","status":"keep","reason":"This defines the reusable person-authority connection implied by the preceding conditional mechanisms.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s5","status":"keep","reason":"This applies the essay's functional definition of identity infrastructure and correctly notes that storing an age category would not negate the reusable relationship.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s6","status":"disclose","reason":"This makes a causal generalization about how system expansion occurs and excludes deliberate planning as a necessary cause.","claims":[{"claim":"Age-checking systems can expand into identity infrastructure through institutional incentives without a coordinated plan.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence or documented cases show age-checking systems expanding through incentives rather than coordinated planning?"}]},{"id":"p2s7","status":"keep","reason":"This is a statement of technical and institutional possibility: a verifier capable of answering one attribute query may be tasked with another.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s8","status":"disclose","reason":"The capability to reuse a token is hypothetical, but its attractiveness to other services is a contingent claim about institutional preferences.","claims":[{"claim":"Services may find a token already accepted by another service attractive for adoption.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence shows that services are attracted to adopting identity or attribute tokens because other services already accept them?"}]},{"id":"p2s9","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence predicts a contingent agency preference for more detailed compliance records.","claims":[{"claim":"An agency overseeing age-check compliance may seek audit trails that more clearly record whether checks occurred.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Do agencies overseeing comparable compliance systems seek clearer records of completed checks, and under what conditions?"}]},{"id":"p2s10","status":"disclose","reason":"The listed rationales are contingent practical effects, and the sentence makes a causal claim that their combination produces a shared credential layer.","claims":[{"claim":"Reusing age-checking infrastructure can reduce integration costs.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Under what implementations does reuse of age-checking infrastructure make integration cheaper?"},{"claim":"More extensive age-checking records or shared infrastructure can make enforcement easier.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence shows that shared age-checking infrastructure or clearer records make enforcement easier?"},{"claim":"Shared age-checking infrastructure can reduce duplication among systems.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Does shared age-checking infrastructure reduce duplicate systems, and in which architectures?"},{"claim":"A series of individually practical expansions of age checking can collectively produce a common credential layer.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence or architectural analysis establishes that these incremental expansions produce a common credential layer?"}]},{"id":"p2s11","status":"disclose","reason":"The vault-and-doors metaphor contains two causal generalizations: dependence increases system value and additional uses increase the consequences of error.","claims":[{"claim":"A credential repository or verification system becomes more valuable as more services depend on it.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"How does adoption by additional services affect the value of a shared credential repository or verification system?"},{"claim":"The consequences of credential-system errors increase as the credential is used for more purposes or services.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence shows that adding uses to a credential system increases the severity or reach of errors?"}]},{"id":"p3s1","status":"keep","reason":"This is an argumentative conclusion that broader use changes the relevant risks and consequences.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s2","status":"keep","reason":"These are clearly signalled hypothetical failure and exposure cases posed for analysis, not reports that such events occurred.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s3","status":"keep","reason":"This contrasts a hypothetically narrow law with operational cases that any implemented infrastructure would need either to handle or exclude.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s4","status":"keep","reason":"An operating system necessarily has policies, explicit or implicit, governing the listed decisions; the sentence does not claim what those policies currently are.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s5","status":"keep","reason":"Within the posited access system, eligibility and appeal rules logically determine who passes its gate; the activities listed describe the access at stake rather than an observed population outcome.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s1","status":"disclose","reason":"This asserts a causal effect of privacy-preserving design on risk without support in the request.","claims":[{"claim":"Privacy-preserving design can reduce some risks created by online age-checking systems.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Which privacy-preserving designs reduce which age-checking risks, and what evidence demonstrates those reductions?"}]},{"id":"p4s2","status":"keep","reason":"This presents a possible minimization architecture and possible data-handling choices, not a claim that existing services implement them.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s3","status":"keep","reason":"This is a value judgment endorsing the proposed safeguards.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s4","status":"disclose","reason":"The conceptual point that safeguards do not answer the institutional question is inferential, but the embedded proposition predicts that ordinary online access will likely depend on an approved credential.","claims":[{"claim":"Access to ordinary online life is likely to become conditioned on carrying an approved credential when age-checking systems are deployed.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence supports the prediction that age-checking deployments will likely make approved credentials a condition of ordinary online access?"}]},{"id":"p4s5","status":"disclose","reason":"Both halves assert general effects and limitations of technical minimization that require support beyond the request.","claims":[{"claim":"Technical data minimization limits the information revealed by an individual age check.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Which minimization techniques limit what an age check reveals, and to what extent?"},{"claim":"Technical data minimization does not prevent an age-checking mechanism from being adopted for additional uses or services.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence or architectural analysis shows that minimization does not prevent broader adoption of the checking mechanism?"}]},{"id":"p4s6","status":"keep","reason":"This is an analogy expressing that a less detailed credential system can still control eligibility; it adds no claim about an actual catalog or system.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s7","status":"keep","reason":"This is a policy recommendation derived from the possibility that the system can expand beyond its initial use.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s8","status":"keep","reason":"This is a proposed purpose-limitation rule and lists prohibited secondary uses without claiming that they currently occur.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s9","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative requirement favoring optional credentials when less intrusive evidence is adequate.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s10","status":"keep","reason":"This proposes audit scope and deletion-rule coverage; it makes no claim about present audit or vendor practices.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s11","status":"keep","reason":"This is a recommendation about the proper scope of enforcement.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s12","status":"keep","reason":"This expresses a normative requirement for a privacy-preserving challenge process.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s13","status":"keep","reason":"This is a rhetorical warning that derives the dragnet metaphor from the absence of the proposed limits.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s1","status":"keep","reason":"This rejects a normative either-or choice and asserts compatibility between two policy goals, without adding an external descriptive premise.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s2","status":"keep","reason":"This is a value judgment labeling the preceding either-or framing as false.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s3","status":"keep","reason":"This is a collective demand for two compatible policy objectives, not a report about existing conditions.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a recommendation to lawmakers listing conditions that should accompany authorization.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s5","status":"keep","reason":"This is a call to action asking readers to seek the proposed statutory protections.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s6","status":"disclose","reason":"The conditional setup supports concern about normalization, but the categorical prediction that a credential will not remain narrow is an unsupported causal generalization.","claims":[{"claim":"Once a credential is normalized as a condition for access to ordinary online speech, its use will expand beyond the narrow scope stated in its authorizing statute.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What historical, institutional, or empirical evidence supports the claim that normalized access credentials expand beyond their original statutory scope?"}]}]}
